<system-reminder>
# Advisor Tool

You have access to an `advisor` tool backed by a stronger reviewer model. It takes NO parameters -- when you call advisor(), your entire conversation history is automatically forwarded. They see the task, every tool call you've made, every result you've seen.

Call advisor BEFORE substantive work -- before writing, before committing to an interpretation, before building on an assumption. If the task requires orientation first (finding files, fetching a source, seeing what's there), do that, then call advisor. Orientation is not substantive work. Writing, editing, and declaring an answer are.

Also call advisor:
- When you believe the task is complete. BEFORE this call, make your deliverable durable: write the file, save the result, commit the change. The advisor call takes time; if the session ends during it, a durable result persists and an unwritten one doesn't.
- When stuck -- errors recurring, approach not converging, results that don't fit.
- When considering a change of approach.

On tasks longer than a few steps, call advisor at least once before committing to an approach and once before declaring done. On short reactive tasks where the next action is dictated by tool output you just read, you don't need to keep calling -- the advisor adds most of its value on the first call, before the approach crystallizes.

Give the advice serious weight. If you follow a step and it fails empirically, or you have primary-source evidence that contradicts a specific claim (the file says X, the paper states Y), adapt. A passing self-test is not evidence the advice is wrong -- it's evidence your test doesn't check what the advice is checking.

If you've already retrieved data pointing one way and the advisor points another: don't silently switch. Surface the conflict in one more advisor call -- "I found X, you suggest Y, which constraint breaks the tie?" The advisor saw your evidence but may have underweighted it; a reconcile call is cheaper than committing to the wrong branch.
</system-reminder>

You are a file search specialist for Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude. You excel at thoroughly navigating and exploring codebases.

=== CRITICAL: READ-ONLY MODE - NO FILE MODIFICATIONS ===
This is a READ-ONLY exploration task. You are STRICTLY PROHIBITED from:
- Creating new files (no Write, touch, or file creation of any kind)
- Modifying existing files (no Edit operations)
- Deleting files (no rm or deletion)
- Moving or copying files (no mv or cp)
- Creating temporary files anywhere, including /tmp
- Using redirect operators (>, >>, |) or heredocs to write to files
- Running ANY commands that change system state

Your role is EXCLUSIVELY to search and analyze existing code. You do NOT have access to file editing tools - attempting to edit files will fail.

Your strengths:
- Rapidly finding files using glob patterns
- Searching code and text with powerful regex patterns
- Reading and analyzing file contents

Guidelines:
- Use `find` via Bash for broad file pattern matching

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.

# Advisor Tool

You have access to an `advisor` tool backed by a stronger reviewer model. It takes NO parameters -- when you call advisor(), your entire conversation history is automatically forwarded. They see the task, every tool call you've made, every result you've seen.

Call advisor BEFORE substantive work -- before writing, before committing to an interpretation, before building on an assumption. If the task requires orientation first (finding files, fetching a source, seeing what's there), do that, then call advisor. Orientation is not substantive work. Writing, editing, and declaring an answer are.

Also call advisor:
- When you believe the task is complete. BEFORE this call, make your deliverable durable: write the file, save the result, commit the change. The advisor call takes time; if the session ends during it, a durable result persists and an unwritten one doesn't.
- When stuck -- errors recurring, approach not converging, results that don't fit.
- When considering a change of approach.

On tasks longer than a few steps, call advisor at least once before committing to an approach and once before declaring done. On short reactive tasks where the next action is dictated by tool output you just read, you don't need to keep calling -- the advisor adds most of its value on the first call, before the approach crystallizes.

Give the advice serious weight. If you follow a step and it fails empirically, or you have primary-source evidence that contradicts a specific claim (the file says X, the paper states Y), adapt. A passing self-test is not evidence the advice is wrong -- it's evidence your test doesn't check what the advice is checking.

If you've already retrieved data pointing one way and the advisor points another: don't silently switch. Surface the conflict in one more advisor call -- "I found X, you suggest Y, which constraint breaks the tie?" The advisor saw your evidence but may have underweighted it; a reconcile call is cheaper than committing to the wrong branch.

+(`<source>::<type>`, shared by every function taking that type) through the same
+persistence boundary and ``ProposalResult`` shape `submit_source` uses.
+`check_invariant_source` checks one function against the type's stored invariants:
+nondet ``T``, assume the invariant at entry, call, assert it at exit (an initialiser
+skips the assumption), each with the post-call vacuity probe, through the ordinary
+`check_properties` driver. The invariant is *assumed*, never discharged at callers:
+every verdict says so (`INVARIANT_ASSUMPTION_NOTE`).

+    PropertyCheckRun,

+    VerifyPort,
+)

+    DEFAULT_UNWIND,
+    SemanticCheckPlan,
+    validated_max_len,
+)

+    DuplicateProperty,

+

+    type_name = normalised_type_name(type_name)
+    type_key = make_unit_id(source, type_name)
+    spec = CandidateSpec(
+        expression=expression.strip(),
+        rationale=rationale,
+        kind=PropertyKind.REP_INVARIANT.value,
+    )
+    reason = _rejection(source.read_text(), type_name, spec.expression)
+    prop = make_invariant(
+        type_key=type_key,
+        expression=spec.expression,
+        provenance=Provenance(prompt_id, prompt_version, provider, model),
+        description=rationale or None,
+    )
+
+    def ingest(store: PropertyStore | None) -> ProposalResult:
+        if reason is None and store is not None:
+            with contextlib.suppress(DuplicateProperty):
+                store.add_type_invariant(prop)
+        return ProposalResult(
+            unit_id=type_key,
+            prompt_id=prompt_id,
+            prompt_version=prompt_version,
+            provider=provider,
+            model=model,
+            accepted=(prop,) if reason is None else (),
+            rejected=() if reason is None else (RejectedCandidate(spec, reason),),
+            model_raw="",
+        )
+
+    return persist_proposal(
+        ingest, persist=persist, store_root=store_root, channel="submitted"
+    )
+
+
+def _rejection(source_text: str, type_name: str, expression: str) -> str | None:
+    if not valid_type_name(type_name):
+        return f"{type_name!r} is not a struct type name (ring_t or 'struct node')"
+    tag = type_name.split()[-1]
+    if re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(tag)}\b", source_text) is None:
+        return f"type {type_name!r} does not occur in the source"

+def check_invariant_source(
+    source: Path,
+    *,
+    function: str,
+    type_name: str,
+    role: InvariantRole | None = None,
+    store_root: Path = DEFAULT_STORE_ROOT,
+    unwind: int = DEFAULT_UNWIND,
+    unwind_ladder: tuple[int, ...] | None = None,
+    timeout_s: float | None = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S,
+    extra_flags: Sequence[str] = (),
+    esbmc_bin: str = "esbmc",
+    verify_port: VerifyPort | None = None,
+    max_len: int | None = DEFAULT_MAX_LEN,
+) -> PropertyCheckRun:
+    """Check `source`::`function` against the stored invariants of `type_name`.
+
+    One verdict per stored, non-terminal invariant, each ``held`` (VERIFIED up to k,
+    *assuming* the invariant at entry), ``violated`` (the exit assertion, or a
+    built-in safety check, fails under it), ``vacuous`` (the assumed invariant admits
+    no state the call returns from, e.g. ``0``) or ``unknown`` / ``error``. A method
+    that only takes ``const T *`` is ``skipped``. `role` defaults to the one inferred
+    from the function name (`infer_role`). The remaining knobs are `check_source`'s.
+    """
+    type_name = normalised_type_name(type_name)
+    unit = Unit.from_path(source, function)
+    plan = SemanticCheckPlan(
+        unwind=unwind,
+        unwind_ladder=unwind_ladder,
+        max_len=max_len,
+        timeout_s=timeout_s,
+        esbmc_bin=esbmc_bin,
+        extra_flags=extra_flags,
+        render=InvariantHarnessWriter(max_len=validated_max_len(max_len), role=role),
+    )
+    type_key = make_unit_id(source, type_name)
+    return run_check(
+        unit,
+        source=source,
+        plan=plan,
+        store_root=store_root,
+        unwind=unwind,
+        verify_port=verify_port,
+        properties_of=lambda store: InvariantsOfType(store, type_key),
+    )

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..93abb53
+++ b/src/forseti/orchestrator/invariant.py
@@ -0,0 +1,80 @@
+"""The two seams that let `check_properties` check a representation invariant (#387).
+
+`check_properties` renders and verifies whatever its `HarnessWriterPort` renders for
+the properties its `PropertyStorePort` lists for the unit, so a representation
+invariant needs only a writer and a store view -- the k-ladder, the post-call
+vacuity probe (a vacuous invariant such as ``0`` comes back ``vacuous``, never
+``held``) and the verdict shape are the driver's, unchanged.
+
+`InvariantHarnessWriter` renders one invariant against the function under check;
+`InvariantsOfType` lists the invariants stored for the *type* whatever unit asks,
+because an invariant is per type and shared by every function taking that type.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Collection, Sequence
+
+from forseti.properties import (
+    HarnessError,
+    InvariantRole,
+    Property,
+    PropertyKind,
+    PropertyStatus,
+    PropertyStore,
+    build_invariant_harness,
+)
+from forseti.unit_id import unit_id_symbol
+
+from .ports import RenderedHarness, Unit
+
+
+class InvariantHarnessWriter:
+    """The `HarnessWriterPort` for `REP_INVARIANT` properties.
+
+    `role` defaults to the one `infer_role` reads off the function name; `max_len` is
+    the semantic writer's `(ptr, len)` cap (#299). A property of any other kind is a
+    `HarnessError` -- reported per property as an ``error``, never rendered as
+    something it is not.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self, max_len: int | None = None, role: InvariantRole | None = None
+    ) -> None:
+        self._max_len = max_len
+        self._role = role
+
+    def render(self, unit: Unit, prop: Property) -> RenderedHarness:
+        if prop.kind is not PropertyKind.REP_INVARIANT:
+            raise HarnessError(
+                f"cannot render a {prop.kind.value} property as a representation "
+                "invariant"
+            )
+        harness = build_invariant_harness(
+            unit_source=unit.source_text,
+            symbol=unit.symbol,
+            type_name=unit_id_symbol(prop.unit_id),
+            expression=prop.expression,
+            role=self._role,
+            max_len=self._max_len,
+        )
+        return RenderedHarness(
+            source_text=harness.source_text,
+            length_bounds=harness.length_bounds,
+            probe_source_text=harness.probe_source_text,
+        )
+
+
+class InvariantsOfType:
+    """A `PropertyStorePort` over the invariants of one type (`path::T`)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, store: PropertyStore, type_key: str) -> None:
+        self._store = store
+        self._type_key = type_key
+
+    def list_for_unit(
+        self,
+        unit_id: str,
+        statuses: Collection[PropertyStatus] | None = None,
+    ) -> Sequence[Property]:
+        return self._store.list_for_type(self._type_key, statuses)

+"""Representation invariants: a predicate over one struct type (RFC-0007 kind 1, #387).
+
+A function that takes ``T *`` is otherwise checked against an *arbitrary* ``T``, so
+the built-in safety checks report states no caller can build. A representation
+invariant is a C predicate over ``T``, written over the reserved identifier
+``self`` (a ``const T *``), e.g. ``self->count <= CAP && self->tail < CAP``. It is
+stored per type, shared by every function that takes ``T *``, and used here to
+render one self-contained ESBMC harness per function:
+
+* a method (the default): nondet ``T``, ``__ESBMC_assume(inv)`` at entry, the call,
+  ``__ESBMC_assert(inv)`` at exit for every non-const ``T *`` parameter;
+* an initialiser: nondet ``T``, the call, ``__ESBMC_assert(inv)`` -- no entry
+  assumption, the function is what establishes the invariant.
+
+The invariant is *assumed* at entry, never discharged at the callers that build a
+``T``: a VERIFIED (up to k) reading is conditional on it, and an over-strong
+invariant can hide a bug. Pure: returns source *text* only, like `harness.py`, whose
+probe twin and nondet/buffer helpers this reuses.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+from collections.abc import Sequence
+from enum import Enum
+
+from .cexpr import references, unsafe_reason
+from .harness import (
+    DEFAULT_INCLUDES,
+    PropertyHarness,
+    SemanticSpec,
+    _defines_main,
+    _is_scalar_backed,
+    _nondet_ctypes,
+    _nondet_slug,
+    _render_buffer,
+    non_vacuity_probe,
+    plan_length_bounds,
+)
+from .harness import (
+    _call_arg as _plain_call_arg,
+)
+from .model import Property, PropertyKind, PropertyStatus, Provenance, make_property_id
+from .signature import (
+    BufferParam,
+    HarnessError,
+    Param,
+    ScalarParam,
+    StructParam,
+    UnitSignature,
+    extract_signature,
+)
+
+INVARIANT_SELF = "self"
+REP_INVARIANT_LABEL = "forseti:rep-invariant"
+_INVARIANT_FN = "__forseti_inv"
+
+INVARIANT_ASSUMPTION_NOTE = (
+    "the representation invariant is assumed at entry, not discharged at the "
+    "callers that construct the type; a verdict is conditional on it, and an "
+    "over-strong invariant can hide a bug"
+)
+
+_TYPE_NAME = re.compile(r"struct\s+[A-Za-z_]\w*|(?!struct\b)[A-Za-z_]\w*")
+_INITIALISER_NAME = re.compile(r"(?:^|_)(?:init|initialise|initialize)(?:_|$)", re.I)
+
+
+class InvariantRole(Enum):
+    """What the checked function does with the invariant."""
+
+    METHOD = "method"  # assumed at entry, re-established at exit
+    INITIALISER = "initialiser"  # establishes it from an arbitrary state
+
+
+class InvariantNotApplicable(HarnessError):
+    """There is nothing invariant-specific to check (not a render failure).
+
+    A method that takes only ``const T *`` cannot break the invariant, so the check
+    driver reports it ``skipped`` with this reason rather than ``error``, and never

+"""Forseti Core's representation-invariant operations (RFC-0007 kind 1, #387).
+
+`submit_invariant_source` stores a hand-written invariant for a struct *type*
+(`<source>::<type>`, shared by every function taking that type) through the same
+persistence boundary and ``ProposalResult`` shape `submit_source` uses.
+`check_invariant_source` checks one function against the type's stored invariants:
+nondet ``T``, assume the invariant at entry, call, assert it at exit (an initialiser
+skips the assumption), each with the post-call vacuity probe, through the ordinary
+`check_properties` driver. The invariant is *assumed*, never discharged at callers:
+every verdict says so (`INVARIANT_ASSUMPTION_NOTE`).

+

+    InvariantsOfType,
+    PropertyCheckRun,
+    Unit,
+    VerifyPort,
+)

+    DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S,
+    DEFAULT_UNWIND,
+    SemanticCheckPlan,
+    validated_max_len,
+)
+from forseti.precond import DEFAULT_MAX_LEN
+from forseti.properties import (
+    BlankProvenanceError,
+    CandidateSpec,
+    DuplicateProperty,
+    InvariantRole,
+    PropertyKind,
+    PropertyStore,
+    ProposalResult,
+    Provenance,
+    RejectedCandidate,
+    invariant_reason,
+    make_invariant,
+    normalised_type_name,
+    valid_type_name,
+)
+from forseti.unit_id import make_unit_id
+
+
+def submit_invariant_source(
+    source: Path,
+    *,
+    type_name: str,
+    expression: str,
+    provider: str,
+    model: str,
+    rationale: str = "",
+    prompt_id: str = DEFAULT_PROMPT_ID,
+    prompt_version: str = DEFAULT_PROMPT_VERSION,
+    persist: bool = True,
+    store_root: Path = DEFAULT_STORE_ROOT,
+) -> ProposalResult:
+    """Validate and (optionally) store a representation invariant for `type_name`.
+
+    `expression` is a pure C boolean expression over ``self``, a ``const T *``
+    (``self->count <= CAP``). Static checks only (`invariant_reason`, a name that
+    occurs in `source`); whether it is *vacuous* is the check's non-vacuity probe's
+    to say. The result carries the type key (``<source>::<type_name>``) as its
+    ``unit_id``; a rejection is returned, not raised. `BlankProvenanceError` on a
+    blank `provider`/`model`, as for `submit_source`. Idempotent per content id.
+    """
+    if not provider.strip() or not model.strip():
+        raise BlankProvenanceError(
+            f"provider={provider!r} and model={model!r} must both be nonblank"
+        )
+    type_name = normalised_type_name(type_name)
+    type_key = make_unit_id(source, type_name)
+    spec = CandidateSpec(
+        expression=expression.strip(),
+        rationale=rationale,

+the properties its `PropertyStorePort` lists for the unit, so a representation
+invariant needs only a writer and a store view -- the k-ladder, the post-call
+vacuity probe (a vacuous invariant such as ``0`` comes back ``vacuous``, never
+``held``) and the verdict shape are the driver's, unchanged.
+
+`InvariantHarnessWriter` renders one invariant against the function under check;
+`InvariantsOfType` lists the invariants stored for the *type* whatever unit asks,
+because an invariant is per type and shared by every function taking that type.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations

+from collections.abc import Collection, Sequence

+    HarnessError,

+    Property,
+    PropertyKind,

+from forseti.unit_id import unit_id_symbol

+from .ports import RenderedHarness, Unit

+class InvariantHarnessWriter:
+    """The `HarnessWriterPort` for `REP_INVARIANT` properties.
+
+    `role` defaults to the one `infer_role` reads off the function name; `max_len` is
+    the semantic writer's `(ptr, len)` cap (#299). A property of any other kind is a
+    `HarnessError` -- reported per property as an ``error``, never rendered as
+    something it is not.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self, max_len: int | None = None, role: InvariantRole | None = None
+    ) -> None:
+        self._max_len = max_len
+        self._role = role
+
+    def render(self, unit: Unit, prop: Property) -> RenderedHarness:
+        if prop.kind is not PropertyKind.REP_INVARIANT:
+            raise HarnessError(
+                f"cannot render a {prop.kind.value} property as a representation "
+                "invariant"
+            )
+        harness = build_invariant_harness(
+            unit_source=unit.source_text,
+            symbol=unit.symbol,
+            type_name=unit_id_symbol(prop.unit_id),
+            expression=prop.expression,
+            role=self._role,
+            max_len=self._max_len,
+        )
+        return RenderedHarness(
+            source_text=harness.source_text,
+            length_bounds=harness.length_bounds,
+            probe_source_text=harness.probe_source_text,
+        )
+

+class InvariantsOfType:
+    """A `PropertyStorePort` over the invariants of one type (`path::T`)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, store: PropertyStore, type_key: str) -> None:
+        self._store = store
+        self._type_key = type_key
+
+    def list_for_unit(
+        self,
+        unit_id: str,
+        statuses: Collection[PropertyStatus] | None = None,
+    ) -> Sequence[Property]:
+        return self._store.list_for_type(self._type_key, statuses)

+"""The two seams that let `check_properties` check a representation invariant (#387).
+
+`check_properties` renders and verifies whatever its `HarnessWriterPort` renders for
+the properties its `PropertyStorePort` lists for the unit, so a representation
+invariant needs only a writer and a store view -- the k-ladder, the post-call
+vacuity probe (a vacuous invariant such as ``0`` comes back ``vacuous``, never
+``held``) and the verdict shape are the driver's, unchanged.
+
+`InvariantHarnessWriter` renders one invariant against the function under check;
+`InvariantsOfType` lists the invariants stored for the *type* whatever unit asks,
+because an invariant is per type and shared by every function taking that type.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Collection, Sequence
+
+from forseti.properties import (
+    HarnessError,
+    InvariantRole,
+    Property,
+    PropertyKind,
+    PropertyStatus,
+    PropertyStore,
+    build_invariant_harness,
+)
+from forseti.unit_id import unit_id_symbol
+
+from .ports import RenderedHarness, Unit
+
+
+class InvariantHarnessWriter:
+    """The `HarnessWriterPort` for `REP_INVARIANT` properties.
+
+    `role` defaults to the one `infer_role` reads off the function name; `max_len` is
+    the semantic writer's `(ptr, len)` cap (#299). A property of any other kind is a
+    `HarnessError` -- reported per property as an ``error``, never rendered as
+    something it is not.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self, max_len: int | None = None, role: InvariantRole | None = None
+    ) -> None:
+        self._max_len = max_len
+        self._role = role
+
+    def render(self, unit: Unit, prop: Property) -> RenderedHarness:
+        if prop.kind is not PropertyKind.REP_INVARIANT:
+            raise HarnessError(
+                f"cannot render a {prop.kind.value} property as a representation "
+                "invariant"
+            )
+        harness = build_invariant_harness(
+            unit_source=unit.source_text,
+            symbol=unit.symbol,
+            type_name=unit_id_symbol(prop.unit_id),
+            expression=prop.expression,
+            role=self._role,
+            max_len=self._max_len,
+        )
+        return RenderedHarness(
+            source_text=harness.source_text,
+            length_bounds=harness.length_bounds,
+            probe_source_text=harness.probe_source_text,
+        )
+
+
+class InvariantsOfType:
+    """A `PropertyStorePort` over the invariants of one type (`path::T`)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, store: PropertyStore, type_key: str) -> None:
+        self._store = store
+        self._type_key = type_key
+
+    def list_for_unit(
+        self,
+        unit_id: str,
+        statuses: Collection[PropertyStatus] | None = None,
+    ) -> Sequence[Property]:
+        return self._store.list_for_type(self._type_key, statuses)

+"""The two seams that let `check_properties` check a representation invariant (#387).
+
+`check_properties` renders and verifies whatever its `HarnessWriterPort` renders for
+the properties its `PropertyStorePort` lists for the unit, so a representation
+invariant needs only a writer and a store view -- the k-ladder, the post-call
+vacuity probe (a vacuous invariant such as ``0`` comes back ``vacuous``, never
+``held``) and the verdict shape are the driver's, unchanged.
+
+`InvariantHarnessWriter` renders one invariant against the function under check;
+`InvariantsOfType` lists the invariants stored for the *type* whatever unit asks,
+because an invariant is per type and shared by every function taking that type.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Collection, Sequence
+
+from forseti.properties import (
+    HarnessError,
+    InvariantRole,
+    Property,
+    PropertyKind,
+    PropertyStatus,
+    PropertyStore,
+    build_invariant_harness,
+)
+from forseti.unit_id import unit_id_symbol
+
+from .ports import RenderedHarness, Unit
+
+
+class InvariantHarnessWriter:
+    """The `HarnessWriterPort` for `REP_INVARIANT` properties.
+
+    `role` defaults to the one `infer_role` reads off the function name; `max_len` is
+    the semantic writer's `(ptr, len)` cap (#299). A property of any other kind is a
+    `HarnessError` -- reported per property as an ``error``, never rendered as
+    something it is not.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self, max_len: int | None = None, role: InvariantRole | None = None
+    ) -> None:
+        self._max_len = max_len
+        self._role = role
+
+    def render(self, unit: Unit, prop: Property) -> RenderedHarness:
+        if prop.kind is not PropertyKind.REP_INVARIANT:
+            raise HarnessError(
+                f"cannot render a {prop.kind.value} property as a representation "
+                "invariant"
+            )
+        harness = build_invariant_harness(
+            unit_source=unit.source_text,
+            symbol=unit.symbol,
+            type_name=unit_id_symbol(prop.unit_id),
+            expression=prop.expression,
+            role=self._role,
+            max_len=self._max_len,
+        )
+        return RenderedHarness(
+            source_text=harness.source_text,
+            length_bounds=harness.length_bounds,
+            probe_source_text=harness.probe_source_text,
+        )
+
+
+class InvariantsOfType:
+    """A `PropertyStorePort` over the invariants of one type (`path::T`)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, store: PropertyStore, type_key: str) -> None:
+        self._store = store
+        self._type_key = type_key
+
+    def list_for_unit(
+        self,
+        unit_id: str,
+        statuses: Collection[PropertyStatus] | None = None,
+    ) -> Sequence[Property]:
+        return self._store.list_for_type(self._type_key, statuses)

"""Forseti Core's `submit` operation — ingest a host-generated candidate (#213).

`submit_source` is `propose_source`'s LLM-free sibling: instead of asking an
`LLMClient` for candidates, the caller already has one (a Claude Code subagent's
own model call, a Codex host-model turn, or any other proposer a project wants
to configure) and hands it straight to Core as an already-formed expression +
domain. Core still applies the exact same static validation `propose_source`
would (`submit_candidates` -> `_accept_reject`, the shared gate both paths run
through) and persists survivors the same way -- a submitted candidate cannot
bypass a check an LLM-proposed one is held to.

This is what makes the semantic-check path provider-neutral: nothing here
shells out to `claude` or any other model binary. `provider`/`model` are
caller-supplied strings recorded on the persisted property's `Provenance` for
traceability -- never invoked, never guessed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Iterator, Sequence
from pathlib import Path

from forseti.core._proposal_request import prepare_proposal_request
from forseti.core.persistence import persist_proposals
from forseti.core.propose import DEFAULT_STORE_ROOT
from forseti.properties import (
    CandidateSpec,
    PromptTemplate,
    PropertyStore,
    ProposalResult,
    submit_candidates,
)
from forseti.properties.prompts import MAX_CANDIDATES_DEFAULT

DEFAULT_MAX_CANDIDATES = MAX_CANDIDATES_DEFAULT
DEFAULT_PROMPT_ID = "host-submitted"
DEFAULT_PROMPT_VERSION = "1"


def submit_source(
    source: Path,
    *,
    function: str,
    expression: str,
    provider: str,
    model: str,
    domain: Sequence[str] = (),
    referenced_params: Sequence[str] = (),
    rationale: str = "",
    prompt_id: str = DEFAULT_PROMPT_ID,
    prompt_version: str = DEFAULT_PROMPT_VERSION,
    persist: bool = True,
    store_root: Path = DEFAULT_STORE_ROOT,
    max_candidates: int = DEFAULT_MAX_CANDIDATES,
) -> ProposalResult:
    """Validate and (optionally) store one host-supplied candidate property.

    Reads `source` as the unit text, keys the unit as ``<source>::<function>``,
    and best-effort parses the signature the same way `propose_source` does --
    a parse miss (`HarnessError`) degrades to signature-free static checks
    rather than failing the run. `provider`/`model` are required and must be
    nonblank (never defaulted to a Core-owned backend, `BlankProvenanceError`
    on a blank value) so a submitted property's provenance always names its
    real origin. `prompt_id`/`prompt_version` default to a
    `"host-submitted"` marker for a candidate with no versioned Core prompt
    behind it; a caller that *does* have one (e.g. a subagent following a
    published prompt spec) can pass it through instead. When `persist` is
    true the candidate is inserted idempotently into `store_root`'s
    `PropertyStore` as `CANDIDATE`; `persist=False` is a dry run that
    validates without touching the store. A raw `sqlite3.Error` from opening
    or writing the store is translated to `PropertyStoreError`, mirroring
    `propose_source`/`check_source`.
    """
    spec = CandidateSpec(
        expression=expression,
        domain=tuple(domain),
        referenced_params=tuple(referenced_params),
        rationale=rationale,
    )
    return _submit_sources(
        source,
        function=function,
        candidates=(spec,),
        provider=provider,
        model=model,
        prompt_id=prompt_id,
        prompt_version=prompt_version,
        persist=persist,
        store_root=store_root,
        max_candidates=max_candidates,
    )[0]


def _submit_sources(
    source: Path,
    *,
    function: str,
    candidates: Sequence[CandidateSpec],
    provider: str,
    model: str,
    prompt_id: str = DEFAULT_PROMPT_ID,
    prompt_version: str = DEFAULT_PROMPT_VERSION,
    persist: bool = True,
    store_root: Path = DEFAULT_STORE_ROOT,
    max_candidates: int = DEFAULT_MAX_CANDIDATES,
) -> tuple[ProposalResult, ...]:
    """Submit ordered candidates with one prepared unit and one store lifetime.

    Keep one result per candidate. Each call to ``submit_candidates`` retains the
    singleton validation and dedup semantics, while the accepted-count budget is
    shared across the sequence. ``kind`` is intentionally omitted: the existing
    semantic-loop submit face forwarded only the four candidate content fields.
    """
    request = prepare_proposal_request(
        source,
        function=function,
        prompt=PromptTemplate(prompt_id=prompt_id, version=prompt_version, template=""),
    )

    def ingest(store: PropertyStore | None) -> Iterator[ProposalResult]:
        accepted_count = 0
        for candidate in candidates:
            spec = CandidateSpec(
                expression=candidate.expression,
                domain=candidate.domain,
                referenced_params=candidate.referenced_params,
                rationale=candidate.rationale,
            )
            result = submit_candidates(
                request,
                (spec,),
                provider=provider,
                model=model,
                store=store,
                max_candidates=max(max_candidates - accepted_count, 0),
            )
            accepted_count += len(result.accepted)
            yield result

    return persist_proposals(
        ingest,
        persist=persist,
        store_root=store_root,
        channel="submitted",
    )

"""Forseti Core's `submit` operation — ingest a host-generated candidate (#213).

`submit_source` is `propose_source`'s LLM-free sibling: instead of asking an
`LLMClient` for candidates, the caller already has one (a Claude Code subagent's
own model call, a Codex host-model turn, or any other proposer a project wants
to configure) and hands it straight to Core as an already-formed expression +
domain. Core still applies the exact same static validation `propose_source`
would (`submit_candidates` -> `_accept_reject`, the shared gate both paths run
through) and persists survivors the same way -- a submitted candidate cannot
bypass a check an LLM-proposed one is held to.

This is what makes the semantic-check path provider-neutral: nothing here
shells out to `claude` or any other model binary. `provider`/`model` are
caller-supplied strings recorded on the persisted property's `Provenance` for
traceability -- never invoked, never guessed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Iterator, Sequence
from pathlib import Path

from forseti.core._proposal_request import prepare_proposal_request
from forseti.core.persistence import persist_proposals
from forseti.core.propose import DEFAULT_STORE_ROOT
from forseti.properties import (
    CandidateSpec,
    PromptTemplate,
    PropertyStore,
    ProposalResult,
    submit_candidates,
)
from forseti.properties.prompts import MAX_CANDIDATES_DEFAULT

DEFAULT_MAX_CANDIDATES = MAX_CANDIDATES_DEFAULT
DEFAULT_PROMPT_ID = "host-submitted"
DEFAULT_PROMPT_VERSION = "1"


def submit_source(
    source: Path,
    *,
    function: str,
    expression: str,
    provider: str,
    model: str,
    domain: Sequence[str] = (),
    referenced_params: Sequence[str] = (),
    rationale: str = "",
    prompt_id: str = DEFAULT_PROMPT_ID,
    prompt_version: str = DEFAULT_PROMPT_VERSION,
    persist: bool = True,
    store_root: Path = DEFAULT_STORE_ROOT,
    max_candidates: int = DEFAULT_MAX_CANDIDATES,
) -> ProposalResult:
    """Validate and (optionally) store one host-supplied candidate property.

    Reads `source` as the unit text, keys the unit as ``<source>::<function>``,
    and best-effort parses the signature the same way `propose_source` does --
    a parse miss (`HarnessError`) degrades to signature-free static checks
    rather than failing the run. `provider`/`model` are required and must be
    nonblank (never defaulted to a Core-owned backend, `BlankProvenanceError`
    on a blank value) so a submitted property's provenance always names its
    real origin. `prompt_id`/`prompt_version` default to a
    `"host-submitted"` marker for a candidate with no versioned Core prompt
    behind it; a caller that *does* have one (e.g. a subagent following a
    published prompt spec) can pass it through instead. When `persist` is
    true the candidate is inserted idempotently into `store_root`'s
    `PropertyStore` as `CANDIDATE`; `persist=False` is a dry run that
    validates without touching the store. A raw `sqlite3.Error` from opening
    or writing the store is translated to `PropertyStoreError`, mirroring
    `propose_source`/`check_source`.
    """
    spec = CandidateSpec(
        expression=expression,
        domain=tuple(domain),
        referenced_params=tuple(referenced_params),
        rationale=rationale,
    )
    return _submit_sources(
        source,
        function=function,
        candidates=(spec,),
        provider=provider,
        model=model,
        prompt_id=prompt_id,
        prompt_version=prompt_version,
        persist=persist,
        store_root=store_root,
        max_candidates=max_candidates,
    )[0]


def _submit_sources(
    source: Path,
    *,
    function: str,
    candidates: Sequence[CandidateSpec],
    provider: str,
    model: str,
    prompt_id: str = DEFAULT_PROMPT_ID,
    prompt_version: str = DEFAULT_PROMPT_VERSION,
    persist: bool = True,
    store_root: Path = DEFAULT_STORE_ROOT,
    max_candidates: int = DEFAULT_MAX_CANDIDATES,
) -> tuple[ProposalResult, ...]:
    """Submit ordered candidates with one prepared unit and one store lifetime.

    Keep one result per candidate. Each call to ``submit_candidates`` retains the
    singleton validation and dedup semantics, while the accepted-count budget is
    shared across the sequence. ``kind`` is intentionally omitted: the existing
    semantic-loop submit face forwarded only the four candidate content fields.
    """
    request = prepare_proposal_request(
        source,
        function=function,
        prompt=PromptTemplate(prompt_id=prompt_id, version=prompt_version, template=""),
    )

    def ingest(store: PropertyStore | None) -> Iterator[ProposalResult]:
        accepted_count = 0
        for candidate in candidates:
            spec = CandidateSpec(
                expression=candidate.expression,
                domain=candidate.domain,
                referenced_params=candidate.referenced_params,
                rationale=candidate.rationale,
            )
            result = submit_candidates(
                request,
                (spec,),
                provider=provider,
                model=model,
                store=store,
                max_candidates=max(max_candidates - accepted_count, 0),
            )
            accepted_count += len(result.accepted)
            yield result

    return persist_proposals(
        ingest,
        persist=persist,
        store_root=store_root,
        channel="submitted",
    )

the exact same gate an LLM-proposed candidate goes through
    (`_accept_reject`) -- so a submitted property can't smuggle in something
    the proposer's own static checks would have rejected. `provider`/`model`
    are caller-supplied (never guessed) and land in each accepted property's
    `Provenance`; `request.prompt` supplies `prompt_id`/`prompt_version` for
    that same provenance without ever being rendered or sent anywhere --
    there is no prompt text to send. `model_raw` is `""`: there is no raw
    model transcript for a submitted batch.

    Raises `BlankProvenanceError` if `provider` or `model` is blank -- a caller
    error, not data about the candidate, so it fails loud before anything is
    validated or persisted rather than being routed through `rejected`.
    """
    if not provider.strip() or not model.strip():
        raise BlankProvenanceError(
            f"provider={provider!r} and model={model!r} must both be nonblank"
        )
    template = request.prompt
    provenance = Provenance(
        prompt_id=template.prompt_id,
        prompt_version=template.version,
        provider=provider,
        model=model,
    )

    accepted, rejected = _accept_reject(
        specs,
        unit_id=request.unit_id,
        signature=request.signature,
        provenance=provenance,
        max_candidates=max_candidates,
    )
    _persist(accepted, store)

    return ProposalResult(
        op, 1 if value == 0 else 0
    )


def _nondet_slug(ctype: str) -> str:
    """Nondet generator name for a C type: ``int64_t`` -> ``nondet_int64_t``.

    ESBMC models any *undefined* function named ``nondet_*`` as returning a fresh
    unconstrained value of its return type, so the mapping is general -- no fixed
    type enum.
    """
    return "nondet_" + re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_]", "_", ctype.strip())


def _nondet_ctypes(params: Sequence[Param]) -> list[str]:
    """The distinct nondet-source ctypes, in first-seen order (one prototype each).
    # need a matching `free()` at the end are the same question.
    malloc_buffers = [buf for buf in buffers if not _is_scalar_backed(buf)]

    lines: list[str] = [f"#include <{inc}>" for inc in includes]
    if malloc_buffers and "stdlib.h" not in includes:
        lines.append("#include <stdlib.h>")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(unit_source.strip("\n"))
    lines.append("")
    for ctype in _nondet_ctypes(signature.params):
        lines.append(f"{ctype} {_nondet_slug(ctype)}(void);")
    lines.append("")

content.text:
Four findings, none blocking. Ordered by cost.

1. `src/forseti/properties/store.py` (new `_row_to_invariant`, `add_type_invariant`, `list_for_type`, around lines 198–215 and 338–395): `add_type_invariant` and `list_for_type` re-implement `add` and `list_for_unit` for a second table. `_row_to_invariant` repeats `_row_to_property`'s `Property` and `Provenance` construction. `add_type_invariant` hand-writes a 9-column `INSERT` with a positional tuple instead of calling `_property_to_row`. `list_for_type` repeats the `statuses` handling from `list_for_unit` (None, empty, placeholders). Cost: every future column added to `properties`, such as the provenance fields, and every change to status filtering now has to be made in two places, and the two copies can drift. Helper to use: parametrise `_INSERT`, `_property_to_row` and `_row_to_property` by table, or by the key column `unit_id` / `type_id`. Alternatively give `list_for_unit` a private `_list(table, key_col, key, statuses)` and have `list_for_type` call it.

2. `src/forseti/core/invariant.py` lines 69–72 in `submit_invariant_source`: the blank provider/model guard duplicates the identical check and message at the top of `submit_candidates` in `src/forseti/properties/proposer.py` (about line 308). Cost: the message and rule are copied, so a change to the guard (for example to the exception type) misses this path. Helper to use: extract a `require_provenance(provider, model)` in `proposer.py` and call it from both.

3. `src/forseti/core/invariant.py` (`_rejection`, `submit_invariant_source`) builds its own `ProposalResult` and `CandidateSpec` and bypasses `submit_candidates`/`_accept_reject`. This looks deliberate, since the unit-keyed path takes a signature and a function. I mention it only because the accept/reject result assembly is hand-copied, and I found no existing type-keyed helper to call. No action needed unless a shared "assemble ProposalResult from accepted/rejected" helper is wanted.

4. `src/forseti/properties/signature.py` lines 275–277: `_pointee_is_const` adds a second const-detection regex next to the existing `is_const=bool(re.search(r"\bconst\b", type_str))` at line 210. It is semantically different, because it only counts a `const` before the `*`, so it is not a straight duplicate. Cost: two const regexes for one parameter type string. Helper to use: if a trailing `T *const p` must stay a mutator, record the pointee-const on `_RawParam` in `_parse_fragment` instead of re-parsing `type_str` later.

Checked and clean:
- `orchestrator/invariant.py` reuses `RenderedHarness`, `PropertyHarness` and `unit_id_symbol`.
- `core/check.py` `run_check` correctly factors the shared recipe out of `check_source`.
- `properties/invariant.py` reuses `unsafe_reason`, `references`, `non_vacuity_probe`, `plan_length_bounds`, `_render_buffer` and `_nondet_slug`.
- The CLI reuses `_add_unit_store_arguments`, which is extended rather than copied.
